question: A product manager drafts this success criterion for a new Claude-powered ticket triage feature: 'The model should triage tickets well.' A prompt engineer reviews it before evaluation work begins and flags it as unusable for building a test suite. Which revised criterion best fixes the problem using the SMART framework?
options: A) 'The triage model should be reviewed by a senior engineer before every deployment to confirm the categories look reasonable.'
B) 'Achieve at least 90% category accuracy on a held-out set of 5,000 tickets, a 10-point gain over the current rule-based system.'
C) 'The triage model should feel accurate and trustworthy to the support team when they review its category assignments each week.'
D) 'The triage model should use the most recent Claude model available so it stays state-of-the-art as new releases ship.'
correct_answers: B) 'Achieve at least 90% category accuracy on a held-out set of 5,000 tickets, a 10-point gain over the current rule-based system.'
explanations: Incorrect -- a manual pre-deployment review process is a process control, not a measurable success criterion an evaluation suite can score against.
Correct -- this criterion is specific, measurable, achievable, and relevant: it names a concrete metric, a target threshold, a test set size, and a baseline comparison.
Incorrect -- 'feel accurate and trustworthy' is still a qualitative, unmeasured impression rather than a quantitative or well-defined qualitative scale, so it can't drive an automated evaluation.
Incorrect -- tying success to always using the newest model describes an implementation choice, not a measurable outcome the triage feature needs to achieve.
